llm.summary: The skill is not deceptive or exfiltrative, but its CO2 depletion monitor is unreliable enough for a safety-adjacent lab workflow that users should review it carefully before use.

dimensions.detail: The behavior is mostly local and purpose-aligned, but using the tool for automated lab monitoring is not proportionate to the weak input validation and inconsistent prediction model.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No hidden installer, dependency fetch, remote payload, or automatic setup behavior was found; the package contains a markdown skill file and one local Python script.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The documentation says not to use the skill when real-time IoT integration is available, yet it also gives cron, sensor-log, and real-time trigger examples without enough validation, authentication, or failure-handling boundaries.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The artifact does not install persistence by itself, but it explicitly instructs users how to create cron-based recurring checks and log outputs.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is CO2 cylinder depletion prediction for lab incubators, but the shipped script ignores the capacity value while the documentation presents 10L versus 40L capacity as important to prediction accuracy.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Use this only as an advisory training or prototype tool unless the calculation model, units, capacity handling, and input validation are fixed and independently validated. Do not rely on it as the only unattended incubator gas monitor, and do not connect it to cron or paging workflows without separate sensor validation, failure alerts, backup alarms, and manual checks.
llm.findings:
[SDI-4] unexpected: The artifact supports the concern: sensor-log and cron examples conflict with the stated exclusion for real-time IoT integration and are under-scoped for automated monitoring.
[SDI-2] expected: The subprocess example runs the packaged monitor with an argument list and no shell expansion; this is broader than necessary but not hidden or purpose-incompatible.
[SQP-3] unexpected: The mixed Chinese/English labels are a documentation quality issue, not evidence of malicious or high-impact behavior.
[T09] unexpected: Confirmed: non-finite or zero numeric inputs can crash the monitor instead of returning the documented status codes, which can suppress automated alerts.
[other] unexpected: Confirmed: capacity is accepted and displayed but does not affect the depletion calculation, despite documentation saying capacity matters for accurate predictions.
